problem.paragraph: Given $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = (3t^{2} - 2)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + (2t - \sin (t))\mathbf{ \text{j} },$$ find the velocity of a particle moving along this curve.
Given $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = (3t^{2} - 2)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + (2t - \sin (t))\mathbf{ \text{j} },$$ find the acceleration vector of a particle moving along the curve in the preceding exercise.

exercises.paragraph: Given the following position functions, find the velocity, acceleration, and speed in terms of the parameter t.

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {3\cos t,3\sin t,t^{2}} \right\rangle$$
$$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = e^{-t}\mathbf{ \text{i} } + t^{2}\mathbf{ \text{j} } + \tan t\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$
$$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = 2\cos t\mathbf{ \text{j} } + 3\sin t\mathbf{ \text{k} }.$$

exercises.paragraph: Find the velocity, acceleration, and speed of a particle with the given position function.

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {t^{2} - 1,t} \right\rangle$$
$$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {e^{t},e^{-t}} \right\rangle$$ . The graph is shown here:

The position function of an object is given by $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {t^{2},5t,t^{2} - 16t} \right\rangle.$$ At what time is the speed a minimum?

Let $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = r\cosh (\omega t)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + r\sinh (\omega t)\mathbf{ \text{j} }.$$ Find the velocity and acceleration vectors and show that the acceleration is proportional to $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t).$$

exercises.paragraph: Consider the motion of a point on the circumference of a rolling circle. As the circle rolls, it generates the cycloid $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left( {\omega t - \sin (\omega t)} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( {1 - \cos (\omega t)} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} },$$ where $$\omega$$ is the angular velocity of the circle:

problem.paragraph: Find the equations for the velocity, acceleration, and speed of the particle at any time.

solution.paragraph: $$v ( t ) = ( \omega - \omega cos ( \omega t ) ) i + ( \omega sin ( \omega t ) ) j , v ( t ) = ( \omega - \omega cos ( \omega t ) ) i + ( \omega sin ( \omega t ) ) j ,$$ $$a ( t ) = ( \omega 2 sin ( \omega t ) ) i + ( \omega 2 cos ( \omega t ) ) j , a ( t ) = ( \omega 2 sin ( \omega t ) ) i + ( \omega 2 cos ( \omega t ) ) j ,$$ $$speed = \omega 2 - 2 \omega 2 cos ( \omega t ) + \omega 2 cos 2 ( \omega t ) + \omega 2 sin 2 ( \omega t ) = 2 \omega 2 ( 1 - cos ( \omega t ) ) speed = \omega 2 - 2 \omega 2 cos ( \omega t ) + \omega 2 cos 2 ( \omega t ) + \omega 2 sin 2 ( \omega t ) = 2 \omega 2 ( 1 - cos ( \omega t ) )$$

exercises.paragraph: A projectile is shot in the air from ground level with an initial velocity of 500 m/sec at an angle of 60° with the horizontal. The graph is shown here:

What is the approximate maximum height of the projectile?

exercises.paragraph: A projectile is fired at a height of 1.5 m above the ground with an initial velocity of 100 m/sec and at an angle of 30° above the horizontal. Use this information to answer the following questions:

problem.paragraph: Determine the maximum height of the projectile.
Determine the range of the projectile.
A golf ball is hit in a horizontal direction off the top edge of a building that is 100 ft tall. How fast must the ball be launched to land 450 ft away?
A projectile is fired from ground level at an angle of 8° with the horizontal. The projectile is to have a range of 50 m. Find the minimum velocity necessary to achieve this range.
Prove that an object moving in a straight line at a constant speed has an acceleration of zero.

The acceleration of an object is given by $$\mathbf{ \text{a} }(t) = t\mathbf{ \text{j} } + t\mathbf{ \text{k} }.$$ The velocity at $$t = 1$$ sec is $$\mathbf{ \text{v} }(1) = 5\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$ and the position of the object at $$t = 1$$ sec is $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(1) = 0\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 0\mathbf{ \text{j} } + 0\mathbf{ \text{k} }.$$ Find the object’s position at any time.

Find $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t)$$ given that $$\mathbf{ \text{a} }(t) = -32\mathbf{ \text{j} },$$ $$\mathbf{ \text{v} }(0) = 600\sqrt{3}\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 600\mathbf{ \text{j} },$$ and $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(0) = \mathbf{0}.$$
Find the tangential and normal components of acceleration for $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = a\cos (\omega t)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + a\sin (\omega t)\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$ at $$t = 0.$$
Given $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = t^{2}\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 2t\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$ and $$t = 1,$$ find the tangential and normal components of acceleration.

exercises.paragraph: For each of the following problems, find the tangential and normal components of acceleration.

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {e^{t}\cos t,e^{t}\sin t,e^{t}} \right\rangle.$$ The graph is shown here:
$$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {\cos (2t),\sin (2t),1} \right\rangle$$
$$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {2t,t^{2},\frac{t^{3}}{3}} \right\rangle$$
$$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {\frac{2}{3}\left( {1 + t} \right)^{3/2},\frac{2}{3}\left( {1 - t} \right)^{3/2},\sqrt{2}t} \right\rangle$$
$$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {6t,3t^{2},2t^{3}} \right\rangle$$
$$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = t^{2}\mathbf{ \text{i} } + t^{2}\mathbf{ \text{j} } + t^{3}\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$
$$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = 3\cos \left( {2\pi t} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 3\sin \left( {2\pi t} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$

Find the position vector-valued function $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t),$$ given that $$\mathbf{ \text{a} }(t) = \mathbf{ \text{i} } + e^{t}\mathbf{ \text{j} },$$ $$\mathbf{ \text{v} }(0) = 2\mathbf{ \text{j} },$$ and $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(0) = 2\mathbf{ \text{i} }.$$

The force on a particle is given by $$\mathbf{ \text{f} }(t) = \left( {\cos t} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( {\sin t} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} }.$$ The particle is located at point $$(c,0)$$ at $$t = 0.$$ The initial velocity of the particle is given by $$\mathbf{ \text{v} }(0) = v_{0}\mathbf{ \text{j} }.$$ Find the path of the particle of mass m. (Recall, $$\mathbf{ \text{F} } = m \cdot \mathbf{ \text{a} }.)$$

solution.paragraph: $$r ( t ) = ( -1 m cos t + c + 1 m ) i + ( - sin t m + ( v 0 + 1 m ) t ) j r ( t ) = ( -1 m cos t + c + 1 m ) i + ( - sin t m + ( v 0 + 1 m ) t ) j$$

problem.paragraph: An automobile that weighs 2700 lb makes a turn on a flat road while traveling at 56 ft/sec. If the radius of the turn is 70 ft, what is the required frictional force to keep the car from skidding?

Using Kepler’s laws, it can be shown that $$v_{0} = \sqrt{\frac{2GM}{r_{0}}}$$ is the minimum speed needed when $$\theta = 0$$ so that an object will escape from the pull of a central force resulting from mass M. Use this result to find the minimum speed when $$\theta = 0$$ for a space capsule to escape from the gravitational pull of Earth if the probe is at an altitude of 300 km above Earth’s surface.
Find the time in years it takes the dwarf planet Pluto to make one orbit about the Sun given that $$a = 39.5$$ A.U.
